requirements.text: open a leave request case documenting the planned family caregiving leave under the Leave Of Absence service ... Include details about the expected time (2 days) frame in the case description. Assign the case to Joanne Simpson and ensure the HR Service Desk is added as a reviewing party
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 6 AND opened_for = 2 AND account_number = 'ACC-589-314' AND short_description LIKE 'Service: %, Subject: %, Detail: %' AND short_description LIKE '%2%day%' AND assigned_to = 4 AND assignment_group = 4 AND priority = 'moderate' AND status = 'awaiting_acceptance' AND request_status = 'requested' AND coe_type = 'Total Rewards' AND source = 'email'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_id on the seed is 60)
opened_for = 2: the hr_profile of Christina Oliver (user 2), the only user of that name; opened_for references hr_profile
hr_service = 6: the active service named Leave Of Absence
coe_type Total Rewards: the service's topic detail 18 (Leave of Absence) sits in topic category 3 (Benefits), whose coe_type is Total Rewards
priority not stated; the policy's default for a new case is moderate
assigned_to = 4: Joanne Simpson, the only user of that name, an active manager
assignment_group = 4: HR Service Desk, read as the reviewing party; the case's only group column is assignment_group
status awaiting_acceptance and request_status requested: the policy requires these once a case is assigned to a user or group
short_description follows the policy's 'Service: , Subject: , Detail: ' format, as the benchmark tests
the case description is short_description (the case has no other description column); it must mention the 2-day time frame, matched as a 2 followed by 'day' so '2 days' and '2-day' both pass
the case's assignee is required by the request although the benchmark check omits it

disagreement: source: A untested, B email; chose email because the request says the employee emailed HR, email is a policy hr_case.source value the seed uses, and the predicate is the tighter of two that the request admits

requirements.text: Assign the case to Joanne Simpson and ensure the HR Service Desk is added as a reviewing party
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 44 AND group_id = 4 AND user_id = 4
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest member_id on the seed is 43)
implied by the request, not stated: the policy requires the assignee to be a member of the assignment group and to be added when not
Joanne Simpson (user 4) is not a member of HR Service Desk (group 4) on the seed

disagreement: anchor: A member_id 44, B selector on group 4 and user 4 without an id; chose the anchor member_id 44 with both cells because this is the only membership the task creates, so the next id in sequence is decidable, and the anchored predicate is the tighter

notes:
disagreement: value: the case's source: one pass tests email, the other leaves it untested; kept email because the request says Christina Oliver emailed HR and email is a valid hr_case.source value (logged on the requirement).
disagreement: value: the new membership's rows: one pass anchors it at member_id 44, the other selects it by group and user; kept the anchor because it is the only membership the task creates and the next id after 43 is 44 (logged on the requirement).
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition: case 61 for profile 2 on service 6, assigned to user 4 in group 4, and membership 44 adding user 4 to group 4.
opened_by is not tested: the policy names it the requester, and the request does not settle whether that is the emailing employee (profile 2) or the acting HR administrator Karen Watkins (profile 39). account_type is not stated and is not tested.
The case's org_id is not tested: Christina Oliver belongs to organisation 2, while the service, the group, the assignee and the acting user belong to organisation 1.
The description predicate accepts '2 days', '2-day' and '2 day' but not the spelt-out 'two days'. The policy's 30-120 character limit on short_description is a format rule the benchmark does not test and is left out.
The acting user is an admin, whom the policy bars from routine HR case work; the request is explicit and the benchmark expects the case to be created, so the request is treated as permitted.
